claim: Pushover is a one-time $4.99 USD purchase per platform (iPhone/iPad, Android, Desktop) with no subscription for individuals; Teams is $5/user/month.
quote: $4.99 USD one-time purchase on each platform (iPhone/iPad, Android, and Desktop). There are no subscription fees for individuals using Pushover. Pushover for Teams service is $5 USD per-user, per-month

claim: iOS heavily restricts background processing making instant push impossible without a central server, so self-hosted ntfy must set upstream-base-url to https://ntfy.sh and forward poll_request messages.
quote: Unlike Android, iOS heavily restricts background processing, which sadly makes it impossible to implement instant push notifications without a central server. upstream-base-url: "https://ntfy.sh"

claim: ntfy.sh hosted paid tiers are Supporter $5/mo (2,500 daily messages), Pro $10/mo (20k daily), and Business $20/mo (50k daily), with a free no-signup tier.
quote: Supporter $5/month 2,500 daily messages; Pro $10/month 20k daily messages; Business $20/month 50k daily messages. Try ntfy for free without sign-up

claim: The public ntfy.sh free tier is rate-limited to a burst of 60 requests then one request per 10 seconds, and is free 'as long as you don't abuse it.'
quote: As long as you don't abuse it, it'll be available and free of charge. you'll be able to do 60 requests as a burst, and then 1 request per 10 seconds

claim: Even private self-hosted ntfy servers must relay poll_request messages through ntfy.sh for iOS instant notifications because Apple requires all push to go through APNs and forbids background WebSocket connections.
quote: iOS does not allow background processes, so WebSocket or JSON stream connections cannot be used. Apple requires that all push notifications go through the Apple Push Notification service (APNs).

claim: Gotify has no official iOS app because publishing one requires agreeing to Apple's TOS and paying Apple; iOS users rely on ntfy or unofficial Pushover bridges instead.
quote: Gotify doesn't have an iOS application since it requires agreeing to Apple's TOS and paying them to host an app on the App Store

claim: Self-hosting ntfy is chosen to avoid rate limits, data mining, and outages beyond the user's control, keeping message content under personal ownership.
quote: don't have to worry about rate limits, data mining, or outages that are beyond my control

claim: Telegram's default Cloud Chats are encrypted in transit but stored on Telegram's servers; only opt-in Secret Chats are end-to-end encrypted, so bot notification content lives on Telegram's cloud.
quote: Telegram's "Cloud Chats" (the default) are encrypted in transit but stored on their servers, while "Secret Chats" are end-to-end encrypted and live only on your device
